title: Three Channels and the Availability Budget

scenes.tts: Three sodium channels sit in a nociceptor. Which of them builds the spike?
scenes.visual: Title card: Three Channels and the Availability Budget. A nociceptor with three channel symbols in its membrane.
scenes.narration: Three sodium channels sit in a nociceptor. Which of them builds the spike?

scenes.tts: Nociceptor spikes draw on three channels concentrated in these neurons.
scenes.visual: Three channels label themselves in the membrane. Labels: Nav1.7 (SCN9A), Nav1.8 (SCN10A), Nav1.9 (SCN11A).
scenes.narration: Nociceptor spikes draw on three channels concentrated in these neurons.

scenes.tts: Two of them are N A V one point seven and N A V one point eight. The third is N A V one point nine.
scenes.caption: Two of them are Nav1.7 and Nav1.8. The third is Nav1.9.
scenes.visual: Each label brightens in turn, with its gene name beneath it.
scenes.narration: Two of them are Nav1.7 and Nav1.8. The third is Nav1.9.

scenes.tts: The last two are tetrodotoxin resistant. That is how their currents are isolated in a recording.
scenes.visual: Tetrodotoxin molecules plug Nav1.7 while the other two keep passing current. Label: tetrodotoxin resistant.
scenes.narration: The last two are tetrodotoxin resistant. That is how their currents are isolated in a recording.

scenes.tts: Those two carry pore residues that weaken the toxin's grip, so the toxin leaves them conducting.
scenes.visual: A zoom into the outer pore: the toxin's guanidinium group fits the sensitive channel and not the resistant one.
scenes.narration: Those two carry pore residues that weaken the toxin's grip, so the toxin leaves them conducting.

scenes.tts: N A V one point seven and N A V one point eight contribute to the spike itself.
scenes.caption: Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 contribute to the spike itself.
scenes.visual: One action potential, with the upstroke and the shoulder tinted and labelled by channel.
scenes.narration: Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 contribute to the spike itself.

scenes.tts: N A V one point nine mainly sets the resting potential and subthreshold excitability.
scenes.caption: Nav1.9 mainly sets the resting potential and subthreshold excitability.
scenes.visual: Beside the spike, a flat resting trace with a small steady inward arrow pulling it upward. Label: Nav1.9.
scenes.narration: Nav1.9 mainly sets the resting potential and subthreshold excitability.

scenes.tts: Keep two kinds of current apart. A transient current rises and then inactivates within milliseconds.
scenes.visual: A transient current trace: fast rise, fast decay to zero. Label: transient, builds the spike.
scenes.narration: Keep two kinds of current apart. A transient current rises and then inactivates within milliseconds.

scenes.tts: A persistent current stays appreciable while the membrane sits still. Its inactivation is slow or incomplete, not absent.
scenes.visual: A persistent current trace: a small level that decays only slowly over the record. Label: persistent, inactivation slow or incomplete.
scenes.narration: A persistent current stays appreciable while the membrane sits still. Its inactivation is slow or incomplete, not absent.

scenes.tts: N A V one point nine supplies a persistent current. Its slow gating suits a role at rest rather than in the upstroke.
scenes.caption: Nav1.9 supplies a persistent current. Its slow gating suits a role at rest rather than in the upstroke.
scenes.visual: The persistent trace is tagged N A V one point nine, and an arrow points to the resting line rather than to the spike upstroke.
scenes.narration: Nav1.9 supplies a persistent current. Its slow gating suits a role at rest rather than in the upstroke.

scenes.tts: Now the quantity this lesson turns on. Availability is the fraction of sodium channels not already inactivated.
scenes.visual: A field of channel symbols: some drawn as closed and ready, some stamped inactivated. A counter reads the ready fraction.
scenes.narration: Now the quantity this lesson turns on. Availability is the fraction of sodium channels not already inactivated.

scenes.tts: Channels sitting in the inactivated state cannot open when the membrane depolarizes.
scenes.visual: A depolarizing step arrives; the ready channels open and the inactivated ones stay shut.
scenes.narration: Channels sitting in the inactivated state cannot open when the membrane depolarizes.

scenes.tts: Availability depends on the voltage the membrane has been resting at. Hold one voltage long enough and availability settles on this curve.
scenes.visual: The steady-state availability curve appears, availability against voltage, with the equation h(V) = 1/(1 + exp[(V - V halves)/k]) on screen. Label: steady state.
scenes.narration: Availability depends on the voltage the membrane has been resting at. Hold one voltage long enough and availability settles on this curve.

scenes.tts: The curve has a half-inactivation voltage and a slope factor. For N A V one point seven-like channels the slope is about seven millivolts. Other subtypes, especially N A V one point eight, need their own measured curves.
scenes.visual: The midpoint and the slope are marked on the curve. On screen: V halves, k about 7 mV. Label: illustrative Nav1.7-like, tetrodotoxin-sensitive curve, not every sodium channel.
scenes.narration: The curve has a half-inactivation voltage and a slope factor. For Nav1.7-like channels the slope is about seven millivolts. Other subtypes, especially Nav1.8, need their own measured curves.
scenes.caption: The curve has a half-inactivation voltage and a slope factor. For Nav1.7-like channels the slope is about seven millivolts. Other subtypes, especially Nav1.8, need their own measured curves.

scenes.tts: The curve runs downhill. The more depolarized the rest, the fewer channels are left to open.
scenes.visual: A vertical resting line slides rightward along the curve; the ready fraction counter falls as it moves.
scenes.narration: The curve runs downhill. The more depolarized the rest, the fewer channels are left to open.

scenes.tts: Two nociceptors carry the same channels. One rests low, one rests high. Which has more available?
scenes.visual: Two resting lines on the curve, at minus 70 and minus 55 millivolts, with the curve values hidden.
scenes.narration: Two nociceptors carry the same channels. One rests low, one rests high. Which has more available?

scenes.tts: The low one. About two-thirds of those channels are available, against about one-fifth.
scenes.visual: The hidden values appear on the curve: h = 0.67 at -70 mV, h = 0.19 at -55 mV, with V halves = -65 mV, k = 7 mV tagged illustrative Nav1.7-like.
scenes.narration: The low one. About two-thirds of those channels are available, against about one-fifth.

scenes.tts: Now give each neuron the same small depolarization, and hold it there. The low one keeps about three-quarters of its availability.
scenes.visual: Both resting lines step 5 mV positive and settle. Beside the low one: fraction kept, about three-quarters.
scenes.narration: Now give each neuron the same small depolarization, and hold it there. The low one keeps about three-quarters of its availability.

scenes.tts: The high one keeps about half. It was already low on the curve, so the same step costs it proportionally more.
scenes.visual: Beside the high line: fraction kept, about one-half. Caption: this is what the step costs each cell, not which cell fires.
scenes.narration: The high one keeps about half. It was already low on the curve, so the same step costs it proportionally more.

scenes.tts: Those midpoints are illustrative. For a real neuron the midpoint is a measurement, not an assumption.
scenes.visual: The curve dims and a tag lands: illustrative midpoint; the direction holds, the size does not.
scenes.narration: Those midpoints are illustrative. For a real neuron the midpoint is a measurement, not an assumption.

scenes.tts: So depolarization does two opposite things at once. It closes the gap to threshold, and it costs availability.
scenes.visual: Split panel: on the left, the resting line creeping toward a threshold line that is drawn as movable; on the right, the ready-channel counter falling.
scenes.narration: So depolarization does two opposite things at once. It closes the gap to threshold, and it costs availability.

scenes.tts: That is the order to ask in. What happened to the channel, then to rest and availability, then to firing.
scenes.visual: Three numbered cards appear in sequence: channel, resting potential and availability, firing.
scenes.narration: That is the order to ask in. What happened to the channel, then to rest and availability, then to firing.

scenes.tts: Treat availability as a budget, but a reversible one. Channels recover from inactivation when the membrane goes negative again. The budget shows what a step costs, not whether the neuron fires.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: availability is a reversible reserve. A gauge that falls with sustained depolarization and refills when the membrane returns to negative voltages.
scenes.narration: Treat availability as a budget, but a reversible one. Channels recover from inactivation when the membrane goes negative again. The budget shows what a step costs, not whether the neuron fires.
